subject: Post-call: Procurement & Pricing options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - Acme Retail

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Post-call: Procurement & Pricing options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - Acme Retail

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Great to meet you both on the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Call recap (high-level)
- Use case: customer support automation + internal knowledge base for product teams (mixed latency/throughput profile).
- Usage profile: expected bursty peaks during product launches; baseline ~3k reqs/day, spikes up to ~20k/day for short windows.
- Data sensitivity: some PII in support tickets — customer requires SOC 2 + VPC option for restricted data.

Commercial & procurement flags I heard on the call
- Procurement prefers PO (standard for Acme) and an EDI/PO-based payment flow — need to confirm cutover timelines.
- Marketplace option would be ideal for faster procurement (AWS Marketplace was mentioned).
- Preference toward committed pricing if we can agree to predictable units and a clear SLO.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm procurement timeline (target PO date)?
2) Are there any internal constraints on minimum contract term or commit levels?
3) I'll loop in our Sales Ops and Contracts folks to clarify PO flow, marketplace listing, and SOW/contract path.

I'll CCing Marissa (Sales Ops) and Lauren (Contracts) to help lay out the commercial paths: hosted (on-demand / commits), Dedicated (reserved capacity, monthly commits), and Private (VPC/on-prem; enterprise licensing).

I've attached a short pricing overview and draft SOW we can iterate on once procurement confirms PO path.

Thanks — talk soon,
Aditya
Aditya Rao

Subject: Re: Post-call: Procurement & Pricing options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - Acme Retail

Thanks Aditya — good recap. A few clarifications from procurement side: 

- PO timeline: Procurement is targeting April 1 as the earliest issuance date, contingent on final pricing + SOC 2 evidence. Our legal team wants to keep the term to 12 months initially.
- Payment: We prefer PO/net-30. Credit card is only for ad-hoc pilot spend and not suitable for production.
- Marketplace: AWS Marketplace would significantly speed internal approvals. Do you support marketplace procurement and consolidated billing?
- Commit levels: we could consider a 6-12 month commit if there are clear uplift benefits (discount tiers). Minimums will be evaluated by finance but starting conversation: looking at commit equivalence to ~500k tokens/month (ballpark).

Also, can you confirm whether Dedicated would require physical co-tenancy or is it logical isolation on your pools? We want to understand the isolation model for regulated data.

Thanks — I'll loop in procurement@acme-retail.com for formal review.

— Samantha
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Retail
Samantha.Green@acme-retail.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: Procurement & Pricing options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - Acme Retail

Hi all — thanks for the details, Sam. Quick pricing/packaging summary and recommended procurement paths to hit a ~Apr 1 PO: 

1) Hosted (Redwood API - on-demand)
- Best for small pilots / low-touch onboarding.
- Pricing: pay-as-you-go per token, no minimum.
- Commit option: 3/6/12 month commits available with tiered discounts (5-5% depending on commit level).
- PO path: we can accept PO + invoicing via standard contract; takes ~10-15 business days for contracting if we use our standard SOW + Master Services Agreement (MSA).

2) Dedicated (Reserved capacity)
- Best for predictable throughput and stronger isolation guarantees. Logical tenant isolation with customer-reserved GPU pools.
- Pricing: monthly reserved capacity with minimum monthly commit; burst capacity billed on usage.
- Commit: typical minimums for Dedicated start at a 12-month commitment for reserved pools; shorter terms may be possible with scaled pricing.
- PO path: recommend DocuSign + MSA + schedule for reserved capacity; procurement lead time ~10-15 business days depending on legal redlines.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem)
- For highest control & compliance (data never leaves customer network if on-prem).
- Pricing: license + implementation + optional support/managed service fees.
- Procurement: enterprise license + statement of work; longer procurement and implementation timelines (4-8+ weeks).

Recommendations to match Acme needs
- To meet Apr 1 PO: pursue AWS Marketplace for the initial pilot if procurement accepts marketplace terms — fastest for PO and internal approvals. If marketplace is not acceptable for production billing, we can route a PO on our standard MSA + SOW.
- If you anticipate steady volumes and need isolation, consider Dedicated with a 12-month commit — we can propose a discounted commit tier that aligns with your ~500k tokens/month estimate.

Attached: concise pricing matrix and a draft SOW for the pilot. I highlighted the runway for commit discounts and the PO/doc path.

Marissa
Sr. Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Marissa / Aditya —

Thanks for the summary and the SOC2 report. A few procurement clarifications to finalize internal approvals: 
- We will proceed with a PO/net-30 for initial production. Please provide the contract (MSA + SOW) with the billing contact and remit address so we can generate the PO.
- Marketplace is preferable, but legal needs to review marketplace terms; please send the marketplace listing ID and the marketplace contract sample if available.
- Commit: finance will sign up to a 12-month commit if you can provide a pricing cadence and a clear exit/fallback for spikes; also need a clause around data residency and encryption-at-rest keys.

Requested items (actionable)
1) Final MSA + SOW (fillable fields: billing address, remit, billing contact).
2) AWS Marketplace listing ID + marketplace contract sample.
3) Confirm whether Dedicated includes separate KV encryption keys per tenant (we need encryption-key separation).

Target: procurement team needs the contract to be in our hands by 2027-03-22 to issue PO by Apr 1.

Procurement Team
